summary.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
summary.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution (own boilers)
segments.commentary: Own-generated steam was 73.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said it will be the source of future growth, with waste-to-energy boilers at Vapi supporting realisation.

segments.name: Steam trading (purchased and resold)
segments.commentary: Traded steam was 22.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Coal trading has been discontinued as low-margin; two trading agreements (Dahej SEZ, Haldia) are signed and management declined to split margins between generation and trading.

segments.name: Industrial gases / nitrogen
segments.commentary: PSA-based nitrogen plant of 350 Nm3/hr commissioned at Ankleshwar. Management described it as currently small and plans air separation units for LIN/LOX and other gases.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to take utilisation to 60%-65%; newer boilers expected at about 50% in initial months after commissioning.
Steam volume growth of 5%-10% expected at existing locations; company-level 20%-25% volume growth described as 'very comfortably' achievable with new capacity and demand revival.

EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 expected to be maintained for next few quarters; Q2 seasonally weaker due to monsoon; full-year performance expected to be at par with or better than Q1 run-rate (management said 'we will try' to sustain growth).
Finance costs expected to moderate in FY27 as IPO proceeds repay high-cost borrowings.
Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive.

Capacity to rise from 345 TPH to approx. 705 TPH; four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) targeted to go live in FY27; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28; IPO-funded Dahej, Ankleshwar and Panoli by Q1 FY29.
Una (Himachal Pradesh) 300 TPH EPC project: expected 8%-10% clear margin per ton, pass-through to customers, no capex; agreement not yet signed.
capex_capacity: Installed steam capacity 345 TPH, about 70% contracted; expansion to approx. 705 TPH.
Around INR60 crore further capex needed to complete the four under-construction projects; another INR170 crore planned over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects.
Ankleshwar nitrogen PSA plant of 350 Nm3/hr commenced; ASU for LIN/LOX under evaluation with build-own-operate partners as an option.
Una EPC: 300 TPH community boiler, project value approx. INR311 crore incl. GST, funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd; 9% revenue share to be recovered from end customers.
Pipeline network above 60 km across seven industrial areas; management estimates adding pipelines costs 10%-20% of existing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Management attributed volume growth to revival in chemical and pharma demand after weak FY24-FY26; tyre and food processing (Haldia agreement) added as new segments.
Customer contracts tenor 1-10 years with non-exit clauses; fuel cost pass-through predominantly monthly, some quarterly; newer contracts include minimum guaranteed off-take.
Management claims 25%-35% cost saving versus captive boilers using furnace oil, LDO or natural gas; less beneficial for large coal-fired textile users, which may be at par.
Monsoon disrupts operations because fuel is wet and industrial clusters flood; Q2 seasonally weaker.
Realisation per ton improved due to better utilisation and higher waste-to-energy mix at Vapi.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 60%-65% utilisation; newer boilers are expected to run at about 50% in initial months after commissioning. Some capacity is held back for 2-3 years of new demand.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA CAGR guidance of 30%-35% going to be beaten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to maintain the Q1 growth momentum for the full year on both EBITDA and revenue, but said 'We are not saying that we will maintain'.

risks_watch: Utilisation is still 41.40% versus a 60%-65% target; newer boilers ramp only to about 50% in initial months, so margin expansion depends on execution.
Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore; IPO proceeds are expected to reduce high-cost debt, but the timing and extent of finance-cost moderation need tracking.
Q2 seasonality from monsoon (wet fuel, flooded clusters) is expected to dent EBITDA per ton below INR1,000; watch Q2 FY27 print.
Coal trading exit and undisclosed split of margins between own generation and traded steam (22.2% of revenue) limit visibility into core-segment profitability.
Four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) must go live in FY27; about INR60 crore capex remains plus INR170 crore for IPO and Tarapur projects.
Una EPC (INR311 crore, 300 TPH) is not yet signed; the 8%-10% per-ton margin is unconfirmed and depends on fuel price pass-through.
Related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing continue for at least a few quarters; watch the size and terms.
Nitrogen business is small (350 Nm3/hr PSA) and ASU/LIN/LOX plans are under evaluation with no firm capex or partner decision.
key_quotes: So, we feel that the margin levels can be maintained and can be even better going forward.
But yes, we are saying we will try to maintain. We are not saying that we will maintain.
We are a proxy play to chemical industries, and we are seeing benefits out of it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery, utilisation headroom and the EBITDA-per-ton outlook, but cautious on forward commitments: management repeatedly said it will 'try' to sustain growth and declined to disclose margin splits, citing competitive sensitivity. Answers were detailed on the pipeline and government demand, while the Una agreement and nitrogen plans were left unfinalised.
